content:
jamie: Hey team — customer (acme-corp) hit a hard break after our API change. Their TypeScript client now errors with 404 on create calls and TS types complain missing param 'model' vs 'modelId'.

jamie: Repro steps I got from them:
jamie: 1) install @redwood/inference@^2.1.0 (they say they upgraded server)
jamie: 2) run this snippet -> fails
jamie:```ts
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await c.clients.create({ model: 'redwood-7b', input: 'hello' }); // 404 / TS: property 'model' not in type
```

rachel: Customer says it started after their infra team flipped the new hosted routing (no canary). They get 404s and then retries spike.

maria: Thanks — looks like an SDK/server param mismatch. Server uses model_id now (snake or camel?) and some endpoints were namespaced under /v1/llm/clients in the new routing. SDK 2.0 still hits /v1/clients.

sam: @maria can you confirm exact server change? We should pin expected behaviors.

maria: Confirmed with infra logs: deploy-bot: routing v2 enabled at 1788999000. New route prefix: /v1/llm and param renamed to model_id (server accepts both for 2 weeks but we disabled compatibility earlier than planned).

deploy-bot: notice: routing-v2 enabled by infra at 2026-02-14T10:30:00Z (1788999000).

lee: Oof — sounds like we removed compatibility flag too early. Customer hit it because their TS SDK was older. Proposed immediate actions: 1) rollback compatibility toggle OR 2) publish quick patch SDK that maps model -> model_id and hits /v1/llm paths.

maria: I can cut a patch to TS SDK in the 2.x line to add a compatibility shim that rewrites payload and path. Patch will be 2.1.3. ETA 2 hours.

jamie: Can we provide customer a hotfix snippet to unblock now? They are blocked in prod.

maria: Workaround for them (paste into their app) — manually set the path and param names:```ts
// workaround: use raw request helper
await c.request({ method: 'POST', path: '/v1/llm/clients', body: { model_id: 'redwood-7b', input: 'hello' } });
```

maria: Or if they can't change code, have them pin server routing flag or ask us to flip compatibility back for their org.

rachel: I've told the customer the workaround and offered temporary rollback if they prefer. They're trying the raw request now.

jamie: Any telemetry on how many customers hit this?

sam: I checked error logs — about 12 orgs in last 6 hours, small percentage but includes multiple large accounts. I'm opening an incident ticket.

lee: Also add a note to the release notes and internal deploy checklist: never disable legacy param acceptance until SDKs have been published+propagated for 48 hours.

maria: Patch status: created branch sdk-ts/compat-model-param, adding path remap and a deprecation warning to console when model is used. Quick test passes locally. Will open PR in 15m.

maria: Example shim added:```ts
// shim in client.create()
if ('model' in body) { body['model_id'] = (body as any).model; delete body['model']; console.warn('[redwood-sdk] "model" is deprecated, use "model_id"'); }
// also translate path prefix /v1/clients -> /v1/llm/clients if server version >= 2
```

rachel: Customer confirmed raw request succeeded and production traffic reduced. They still want a permanent SDK fix.

jamie: Good. Can we also add an automated integration test so we don't break this again?

sam: Yes, adding a contract test comparing SDK requests to server routing versions. Assigning to eng-qa.

lee: I'll keep compatibility flag on for the next 24h while we publish patch. After patch is published and customer upgraded, we can turn it off.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/pull/482 (draft). Will request review from eng-runtime.

jamie: Thanks everyone — I'll update the customer with the SDK patch ETA and rollback window. :thumbsup:
